values.goal: Design Worker communication contracts and buffer ownership, and measure the costs of cancellation, queues, and recovery.
values.capstone: Build a cancellable array-processing queue and compare correctness, end-to-end latency, and input responsiveness on the main thread and Workers.

values.title: Messages and Execution Boundaries
values.prerequisites: Understand JavaScript asynchronous behavior and TypedArray, and be able to read the inputs and outputs of the existing starting examples.
values.environment: The existing web-workers-01·02·03 are starting examples. Implement the new assignments in main.js and worker.js in a separate local HTTP project. Preserve CSP and iframe isolation. For SharedArrayBuffer, check COOP and COEP requirements on an external server you control; use the transfer path if they are not met. Measure performance yourself.
values.concepts.0.title: Worker context
values.concepts.0.explanation: A Worker runs in a context separate from the main thread. The main side updates the DOM after receiving messages.
values.concepts.1.title: Request identification
values.concepts.1.explanation: Completion order may differ from request order. Keep requestId in inputs, results, and errors.
values.outcomes.0: Learning outcome: explain the role of Worker context. Input cases: IDs and 3 integer arrays.
values.outcomes.1: Deliverable: per-request sums and a record of UI input responsiveness. Explain the rationale for handling Request identification, linking it to the code.
values.steps.0: In src/day-1.js in a separate practice project, create main.js and worker.js and request sums using new Worker and postMessage. Refer to the existing Unit 1·14·28 examples only as starting points.
values.steps.1: Input conditions: IDs and 3 integer arrays. Baseline: 100 elements. Run under the baseline conditions, then record observations and errors in notes/day-1.md.
values.steps.2: Variable: Array length; changed value: 100000 elements. Run again through the same input path. Deliverable to save: per-request sums and a record of UI input responsiveness. Hypothesis to check: Main-thread input handling should remain possible during computation. Compare it with the actual results, and record whether they agree and why they differ.
values.variables.0.name: Array length
values.variables.0.expected: Main-thread input handling should remain possible during computation.
values.criteria.0: Required deliverable: per-request sums and a record of UI input responsiveness. Results are available for both the baseline and changed conditions, allowing comparison of 2 conditions; input values and the execution environment are recorded together.
values.criteria.1: The explanation of differences between the two conditions connects both concepts: Worker context and Request identification. For unexpected items, at least 1 cause or reason they remain unresolved is recorded.
values.questions.0: Which processing stage does Worker context affect in this exercise? Input cases: IDs and 3 integer arrays.
values.questions.1: Variable: Array length. Hypothesis to check: Main-thread input handling should remain possible during computation. Did the actual results agree with the hypothesis? Explain the evidence in terms of Request identification.
values.references.0.title: MDN Using Web Workers
values.references.1.title: MDN Transferable objects

values.concepts.0.title: Module Worker
values.concepts.0.explanation: type:module uses module syntax. Local HTTP and a correct URL are required.
values.concepts.1.title: Loading failure
values.concepts.1.explanation: A script path failure differs from a computation error. Show initialization failures as a distinct UI state.
values.outcomes.0: Learning outcome: explain the role of Module Worker. Input cases: a valid path and a missing path.
values.outcomes.1: Deliverable: a ready state or loading error state. Explain the rationale for handling Loading failure, linking it to the code.

values.concepts.0.title: Tags
values.concepts.0.explanation: type distinguishes message meanings. Interpreting every message as the same data shape causes errors.
values.concepts.1.title: Validation
values.concepts.1.explanation: Values received by a Worker also require validation. Check requestId and the array type before computing.

values.environment: First check the execution scope guidance on the example screen. The following describes the environment needed to extend the assignment in a separate project. values.concepts.0.title: Copying
values.concepts.0.explanation: Ordinary objects sent with postMessage are structured-cloned. Changing the object after sending it does not change the separate received object.
values.concepts.1.title: Cloning limitations
values.concepts.1.explanation: Functions and DOM nodes cannot be cloned in ordinary messages. Handle failures at the sending stage.
values.outcomes.0: Learning outcome: explain the role of Copying. Input cases: an object and a function field.
values.outcomes.1: Deliverable: sent and received values and a DataCloneError record. Explain the rationale for handling Cloning limitations, linking it to the code.
values.steps.0: In src/day-4.js in a separate practice project, send a nested object, modify the original afterward, and also try a message containing a function. Refer to the existing Unit 1·14·28 examples only as starting points.
values.steps.1: Input conditions: an object and a function field. Baseline: Number. Run under the baseline conditions, then record observations and errors in notes/day-4.md.
values.steps.2: Variable: Field; changed value: Function. Run again through the same input path. Deliverable to save: sent and received values and a DataCloneError record. Hypothesis to check: Values that cannot be cloned are handled separately as sending errors. Compare it with the actual results, and record whether they agree and why they differ.

values.criteria.1: The explanation of differences between the two conditions connects both concepts: Copying and Cloning limitations. For unexpected items, at least 1 cause or reason they remain unresolved is recorded.
values.questions.0: Which processing stage does Copying affect in this exercise? Input cases: an object and a function field.
values.questions.1: Variable: Field. Hypothesis to check: Values that cannot be cloned are handled separately as sending errors. Did the actual results agree with the hypothesis? Explain the evidence in terms of Cloning limitations.

values.concepts.0.title: View
values.concepts.0.explanation: A TypedArray is a view interpreting an ArrayBuffer. The view and the underlying storage may cover different ranges.
values.concepts.1.title: Offset
values.concepts.1.explanation: subarray points to part of the same storage. Preserve offset and length on the receiving side as well.
values.outcomes.0: Learning outcome: explain the role of View. Input cases: the middle two values of [10,20,30,40].
values.outcomes.1: Deliverable: a table of sent and received ranges and sums. Explain the rationale for handling Offset, linking it to the code.
values.steps.0: In src/day-5.js in a separate practice project, send the full array and a subarray, and print byteOffset, length, and values. Refer to the existing Unit 1·14·28 examples only as starting points.

values.concepts.0.title: Task errors
values.concepts.0.explanation: A computation exception is a failure of an individual request. Distinguish it from a Worker loading or runtime error.
values.concepts.1.title: Cleanup
values.concepts.1.explanation: Remove failed requests from the pending list as well. Other valid requests can continue to be processed.
